extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, law school clinics, inventors, small businesses, and USPTO stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO program descriptions, admission/representation rules, outreach programs, and performance metrics relevant to patent practice, practitioner admission, pro bono services, and public assistance centers. Includes procedural rule changes, program participation counts, and customer-service performance targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pro Bono Program eligibility and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: A nationwide network of independently operated, not-for-profit, regional programs that match volunteer patent practitioners with qualified, financially underrepresented inventors and small businesses to provide pro bono patent application preparation, filing, and prosecution services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program performance in FY2021: helped underrepresented inventors and small businesses file 202 patent applications, fielded 1,920 inquiries, and matched 404 underrepresented inventors and small businesses with volunteer patent practitioners. Over 1,800 registered patent practitioners are available to participate in regional programs. The USPTO recognized over 100 practitioners who donated at least 50 hours of service in calendar year 2020 and recognized 28 law firms. Program outreach conducted to over 80 IP law associations; transitioned to virtual presentations (presented to AIPLA, Invention-Con 2021, IP organizations, and inventor groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: GRB scientific and technical qualification categories for registration exam
rubrics_metrics.description: Three categories of technical and scientific qualifications may make applicants eligible to sit for the registration examination: Category A for specified bachelor’s degrees, Category B for other bachelor’s degrees with technical and scientific training, and Category C for practical engineering or scientific experience. If an applicant does not qualify under any category, the USPTO will conduct an independent review for compliance with the scientific and technical training requirement set forth in CFR § 11.7(a)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on comments and evaluation, USPTO changed criteria to: add common Category B degrees to Category A; accept advanced degrees (master’s and Ph.D.) under Category A; and accept a combination of core sciences under Category B (Options 2 and 4) provided one core science course has a lab component.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR part 11 representation and professional conduct updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule revisions to 37 CFR part 11 (Representation of Others before the USPTO) that align the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct more closely with recent revisions to the American Bar Association Model Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes make compliance with part 11 easier by revising various deadlines and procedures related to the registration exam, reinstatement, and limited recognition; include non-substantive changes to improve comprehensibility. The USPTO also published a final rule eliminating the requirement for original, handwritten signatures in correspondence related to registration to practice before the agency in patent cases, enrollment and disciplinary investigations, and disciplinary proceedings, as well as for credit-card payments where the payment is not made via the USPTO’s electronic filing systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent and Trademark Resource Centers (PTRCs) roles and performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: PTRCs are a nationwide network of public, state, and academic libraries designated to disseminate patent and trademark information and support the public’s diverse IP needs. PTRC library staff are trained information experts who assist entrepreneurs and small business owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTRC assistance includes: aiding users in identifying relevant USPTO resources, using USPTO patent and trademark search tools, referring to USPTO offices and community resources. Each PTRC is located within a government or university-supported library; USPTO provides training/support while host institutions allocate staff, space, and collections. PTRCs faced closures/reduced walk-in services during the pandemic and many offer video-conferencing assistance. The USPTO tracks two PTRC metrics: number of individuals assisted and number of attendees at classes. FY2021: PTRCs assisted 6,787 individuals and had 7,991 class attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventors Assistance Center (IAC) assistance scope and call volume
rubrics_metrics.description: The IAC provides patent information and services to the public (entrepreneurs and small businesses), staffed by former USPTO officials who answer general questions concerning patent examining policy and procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IAC functions: answers questions concerning necessary format and formal requirements for a patent application; assists with proper completion of patent application forms; provides general information on patent examining rules, procedures, and fees; directs callers to appropriate USPTO personnel or resources. IAC receives approximately 26,381 calls per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Assistance Center (TAC) service goals and performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The TAC is the primary support center for all trademark customers, from first-time filers to legal professionals, serving as the primary touchpoint for entrepreneurs and small businesses to obtain information and assistance about trademark application, registration, and maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2021 TAC activity: assisted over 149,000 customers (approximately 69% entrepreneurs/small business owners), answered 116,088 telephone calls, and responded to 33,137 emails. TAC is measured by three key performance goals: answer 85% of telephone calls within 20 seconds of entering the TAC queue; score a 97% call handle rate; achieve an 86% customer satisfaction survey score. TAC also facilitated educational webinars (e.g., 434 entrepreneurs and small business owners attended 'Lunch and Learn' webinars in FY2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Law school clinic participation and performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Law school clinics participating in USPTO programs represent clients in patent and trademark matters and assist with application filings and prosecution on behalf of their clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the period July 2020–June 2021, participating law schools reported filing 151 patent applications and 754 trademark applications, obtained 65 patent grants and 379 trademark registrations on behalf of clients, filed responses in over 287 patent matters and over 692 trademark matters, and represented approximately 2,168 clients. At present, 60 law school clinics participate in the program; applications to admit additional law schools were accepted through Dec 31, 2022. USPTO projects future filings will equal or surpass prior years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional offices outreach, training, and stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO regional offices and the Eastern Regional Outreach Office support, facilitate, coordinate, and lead high-level engagements with community IP leaders and government officials, communicating and carrying out the USPTO mission by providing resources, information, programs, and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional offices create strategic partnerships focused on continuing education of stakeholders (including IP professionals); deliver IP education across skill levels; train and judge law students in the National Patent Application Drafting Competition; train new patent attorneys and agents through the Legal Experience and Advancement Program (LEAP); participate in policy events and host policy-related events (e.g., China IP Road Shows, anti-counterfeiting seminars, STOPFakes programs, USPTO Design Day). Regional offices facilitate industry- and government-specific IP discussions (examples given). In FY2021 all regional programming remained virtual, enabling expanded multi-regional reach. Since Oct 1, 2020, regional directors and the Eastern Regional Outreach Director conducted over 550 one-on-one meetings with stakeholders to gather feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM and invention-education outreach program metrics and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO Office of Education (OE) and Office of Innovation Outreach (OIO), in partnership with organizations like the National Inventors Hall of Fame (NIHF) and the National Academy of Inventors (NAI), provide STEM and invention-education programs for K-20 audiences, teachers, and student inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program examples and metrics: Camp Invention provides STEM enrichment to approximately 150,000 children (grades K-6) and expanded to virtual/hybrid camps in 2021; NIHF education programs had nearly 180,000 student registrations and more than 20,000 teachers participating by mid-2021, with 101,000 students receiving scholarships. The Collegiate Inventors Competition uses two tiers of expert judging (including USPTO examiners and NIHF inductees); winners receive cash prizes and many finalists have gone on to start businesses, license technologies, and continue research. OE develops classroom resources, teacher professional development (e.g., National Summer Teacher Institute), and engages stakeholders to integrate invention education into K-20 curricula.
